title: Book: The Joys of Compounding — Gautam Baid (2020)

text: Indian investor Gautam Baid's book blends investing lessons with habits for life: continuous learning (reading widely), patience and compounding, staying within your circle of competence, thinking in terms of probabilities, keeping emotions in check, and building a margin of safety. It draws on Buffett, Munger and other value investors and applies the ideas to an Indian reader. Takeaways relevant to a beginner: start early, avoid leverage, keep learning and don't confuse a rising market with skill. Caveat: it is oriented to stock investing and concentrated, long-term holding, which is high-effort and risky for a beginner; for most young earners a diversified fund approach is the more practical starting point.
